env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection. Disclose unknown reply timing and do not infer reply links from speaker order alone.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Computation and source suitability:
  - Use code for raw counts, regex/literal matching, supplied numeric columns and fixed
    computational recipes. Use a prompt when the measurement requires understanding meaning.
    Do not add semantic filtering to a raw count or URL detector merely because outcome text
    may occur in its source. Disclose that contamination risk; raw text is not outcome-free.
  - Semantic feature specs must exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome
    resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence of the construct. Generic
    platform/delta-rule discussion remains eligible. Explicitly requested semantic exclusions
    remain part of any measurement; never remove one just to force code.
  - Use current supplied text unless the hypothesis restricts time. Deleting edits does not
    recover initial/pre-outcome text. No supplied comment/edit timestamps establish timing.
    If a required temporal measurement is unavailable, explain it and set term=null.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring a different outcome or an
    outcome-revealing predictor is unsupported: preserve the claim, explain it and set
    term=null rather than substituting another test or a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with lower content word overlap with OP are more persuasive (they bring novel information instead of echoing the OP)

features.name: mean_comment_op_content_overlap
features.definition: On average across counter-argument comments, what proportion of a comment's distinct content words also appear in the OP's title and argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; malformed/missing OC_comments, or missing title and argument, -> null. Empty list -> null. Tokenize text with re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text.lower()). Content words = tokens not in sklearn's ENGLISH_STOP_WORDS (fixed stopword list, an operational stand-in since no POS tagger is specified) and with length>=3. OP set = distinct content words in (title + ' ' + argument) (current text; may include edits/outcome announcements, not filtered). For each comment with at least one content word, overlap = |distinct comment content words in OP set| / |distinct comment content words|. Comments with no content words are skipped. Return the unweighted mean of overlap over comments; null if no comment has content words or the OP set is empty/missing. Each comment is counted equally; list order is ignored.

decomposed.h0: mean_comment_op_content_overlap has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Lower mean_comment_op_content_overlap is associated with a higher probability of delta (negative coefficient).
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: content words = non-stopwords (sklearn list), length>=3, no lemmatization; overlap is lexical type overlap against OP title+argument, a proxy for echoing vs. novel information (novelty itself is not measured). Persuasiveness is operationalized as the delta outcome at row level. Comments are pooled as an unweighted mean; the row-level result cannot isolate the most persuasive comment since no per-comment outcomes exist. Raw text may contain view-change announcements or edits in OP argument or later comments; not filtered, so contamination/timing risk remains. Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that reuse fewer of their own content words from the OP are more persuasive (they bring fresh perspectives)

features.name: counter_content_word_reuse_share
features.definition: What proportion of content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) across the counter-argument comments also appear among the content words of the OP's title and argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of comment strings; malformed/missing OC_comments, title or argument -> null; empty list -> null (no content words). Tokenize with nltk word_tokenize on lowercased text, keep alphabetic tokens, POS-tag with nltk pos_tag (Penn tags) and keep content words: tags starting NN, VB, JJ, RB. Build the OP set from the content-word tokens (same procedure) of title + ' ' + argument. Pool the content-word tokens of all comments (each token occurrence counted). Value = (number of comment content-word tokens whose lowercase surface form is in the OP set) / (total comment content-word tokens); null if the denominator is 0. Do not use conversation.

decomposed.h0: counter_content_word_reuse_share has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher counter_content_word_reuse_share (less fresh vocabulary) is associated with a lower probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: "reuse of OP content words" is lexical overlap of exact lowercase surface forms (no lemmatization), pooled over all counter-comments; the OP vocabulary is the current title+argument text, which may include edits or post-outcome/delta announcements (contamination/timing risk; raw text is not outcome-free). Overlap measures vocabulary reuse only, not whether perspectives are actually fresh; "persuasive" is measured only by the dataset outcome delta. Comment order/timing unknown; comments may include quotes of the OP, which count as reuse mechanically. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cover a smaller fraction of the OPs content vocabulary are more persuasive

features.name: op_vocab_coverage_by_counterarguments
features.definition: What fraction of the OP's distinct content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) also appear in the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; malformed/missing OC_comments, title or argument -> null; an empty list -> null. Tokenize text (lowercase, alphabetic tokens), POS-tag with a fixed tagger (e.g. spaCy en_core_web_sm or NLTK averaged perceptron) and keep content words = tokens tagged NOUN, VERB, ADJ or ADV (Penn tags NN*, VB*, JJ*, RB*), lemmatized, excluding stopwords/auxiliaries by POS only. OP vocabulary V_op = set of distinct content lemmas in title + ' ' + argument (current text). Comment vocabulary V_c = union of distinct content lemmas across all comments in OC_comments. Value = len(V_op & V_c) / len(V_op), in [0,1]. If V_op is empty -> null. Computed once per row over the pooled comments; no ordering used.

decomposed.h0: op_vocab_coverage_by_counterarguments has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Lower op_vocab_coverage_by_counterarguments is associated with higher probability of OP view change (negative coefficient).
decomposed.note: Assumptions: "OP's content vocabulary" = distinct content-word lemmas of title plus argument; counter-arguments pooled across all OC_comments (a row-level pooled measure, not per-comment average). "Persuasive" operationalised as the dataset outcome delta (association only). Coverage is the share of OP vocabulary appearing in comments, so it rises with comment count/length; no control is added. Raw-text code is not semantically filtered: argument may contain edits or delta/view-change announcements and comments may quote the OP, inflating overlap; text timing relative to outcome is unknown. Tagger/lemmatizer choice is an implementation assumption.

decomposed.hypothesis: Longer counter-arguments (more words) are more likely to win delta from the OP

features.name: mean_counter_comment_words
features.definition: What is the mean number of words per counter-argument comment in the row?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as JSON list of strings; if missing or malformed return null; if empty list return null. For each comment, word count = len(re.findall(r'\S+', comment)). Return the mean across all comments in the list. Raw text count, no semantic filtering; comments may contain outcome announcements.

decomposed.h0: mean_counter_comment_words has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher mean_counter_comment_words is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.note: Row-level operationalization: per-comment outcomes are not supplied, so the claim is tested at row level using the mean comment length (comment-level winning comment cannot be identified). Maximum length could be an alternative but mean was chosen. Rows with no comments get null. List order has no meaning; comments may include outcome announcements or later replies, and timing is unknown. Association only, OLS on the binary outcome (linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with longer average words (higher reading complexity) are more persuasive

features.name: oc_mean_word_length
features.definition: What is the average number of characters per word across all words in the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. If malformed/missing return null; if empty list return null. Concatenate all comments' text, extract words with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9']+", text) (case preserved, apostrophes kept), and return total characters in these tokens divided by number of tokens (pooled across all comments). Return null if there are zero tokens. Raw text; includes any quoted text or outcome announcements present in comments.

decomposed.h0: oc_mean_word_length has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_mean_word_length is associated with a higher probability of delta.
decomposed.note: Reading complexity is operationalized only as average word length (characters per word), as the hypothesis states "longer average words"; no readability index is used. Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Pooled over all words in all available comments; comment order and timing are unknown. Comments may contain quotations of others or outcome-related text (e.g., delta mentions), not removed since this is a raw code measure. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with more sentences are more persuasive

features.name: mean_sentences_per_counter_comment
features.definition: What is the mean number of sentences per counter-argument comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. If missing/malformed return null; if the list is empty return null. For each comment, count sentences by splitting on regex (?<=[.!?])\s+ after stripping, dropping empty segments (newline-separated paragraphs also split sentences when non-empty). Return the mean sentence count across comments (sentences per comment).

decomposed.h0: mean_sentences_per_counter_comment has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher mean_sentences_per_counter_comment is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Row-level aggregation by mean sentences per comment is an assumption; the hypothesis does not specify mean vs total or maximum. Sentence splitting is a regex heuristic (abbreviations, lists, and URLs may be miscounted). OC_comments may include comments posted after or containing delta/view-change announcements; raw counts are not outcome-free. Comment order and timing are unknown. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with more paragraphs are more persuasive

features.name: mean_paragraphs_per_counter_comment
features.definition: What is the average number of paragraphs per counter-argument comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads. For each comment string, count paragraphs: split on regex r'\n\s*\n', strip each piece, count nonempty pieces. Return the mean across comments. Empty list -> null; missing/malformed JSON -> null. Raw text count, not semantically filtered; may include outcome announcements or quotations.

decomposed.h0: mean_paragraphs_per_counter_comment has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Higher mean_paragraphs_per_counter_comment is associated with higher likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). "Counter-arguments with more paragraphs" is operationalized as the row-level mean paragraph count per comment; blank-line separation is assumed to mark paragraphs. Comments are unordered, with no per-comment outcomes, so this is a row-level association, not a per-comment effect. Comment length is not controlled. Text may contain outcome announcements (not filtered).

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with URLs or hyperlinks are more likely to win delta from the OP

features.name: any_counter_comment_has_url
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a URL or hyperlink?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings. If missing/malformed, return null. If the list is empty, return 0. Return 1 if any comment matches regex r'(https?://|www\.)\S+' or markdown link r'\[[^\]]+\]\([^)]+\)' (case-insensitive); else 0. Mechanical match, no semantic filtering.

decomposed.h0: any_counter_comment_has_url has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows with a counter-argument containing a URL/hyperlink have a higher probability of delta.
decomposed.note: Row-level test: comments lack per-comment outcomes, so we cannot tell which comment won the delta; this tests whether a row has any URL-bearing counter-argument, not that the specific URL comment earned the delta. Raw text matching may include URLs in delta-award or other post-outcome text (e.g., bot messages); this contamination is not filtered. Comment timing is unknown. Association only; OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with markdown formatting (bold/italic) are more persuasive

features.name: any_counter_comment_markdown_emphasis
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain markdown bold or italic formatting?

decomposed.h0: any_counter_comment_markdown_emphasis has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Rows with counter-argument comments containing markdown bold/italic have higher delta probability than rows without.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the OP changed view (delta) at row level; association only. Comments are not individually linked to outcomes, so the formatted comment may not be the persuasive one. Row-level 'any' is an assumption (alternatives: share of formatted comments). Regex may catch literal asterisks/underscores (e.g., snake_case, lists) and misses formatting stripped from the data. Raw text may contain outcome announcements; no timing information.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with bullet list formatting are more persuasive

features.name: any_comment_bullet_list
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain bullet-list formatting?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings (json.loads). If missing/malformed, return null. If empty list, return 0. Return 1 if any comment contains at least two lines, each matching regex r'^\s*(\\?[-*+•])\s+\S' (multiline, markdown unordered bullet markers, optionally backslash-escaped), else 0. Numbered lists are not counted. Raw text matching only; no semantic filtering.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_bullet_list has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_bullet_list = 1 have a higher rate of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness operationalized as dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Bullet list defined as markdown unordered list with at least two bullet lines; the threshold of two is an operational assumption. Numbered lists excluded. Comments are unordered, per-comment outcomes unavailable, so row-level presence is a coarse measure; the bullet comment need not be the persuasive one. Raw text may include outcome announcements or later replies; the feature is mechanical and not outcome-free. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with explicit ordinal structure markers (first, second, finally) are more persuasive

features.name: share_comments_ordinal_markers
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments contain explicit ordinal structure markers such as first, second, and finally?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. If missing or malformed, return null; if the list is empty return null. For each comment, lowercase and find distinct markers among the word-boundary regex groups: first|firstly|1st; second|secondly|2nd; third|thirdly|3rd; finally|lastly|last but not least. A comment counts as 1 if it contains at least two distinct marker groups (so a sequence, not a single incidental 'first'), else 0. Return the sum of counted comments divided by number of comments. Raw literal matching, no semantic filtering; quoted text and OP-quoted text inside comments is not excluded.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_ordinal_markers has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_ordinal_markers is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (association only). Operational assumptions: 'explicit ordinal structure' means at least two distinct ordinal markers in one comment; the regex may match non-structural uses (e.g. 'first time', 'second amendment'), and can miss numbered lists or other enumerations. Share across comments is used because comments are not individually outcome-labeled; list order has no meaning. Comment text may contain outcome announcements or later replies; raw regex is not outcome-free and timing is unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with example phrases (for example, for instance, e.g.) are more persuasive

features.name: example_phrase_comment_count
features.definition: How many counter-argument comments contain an example phrase such as 'for example', 'for instance' or 'e.g.'?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; malformed/missing -> null; empty list -> 0. Count comments where case-insensitive regex r'\b(for example|for instance|e\.g\.?)' matches (also 'e.g.' with trailing punctuation/comma). Return the integer count. Raw text matching with no semantic filtering; matches inside quotations or outcome announcements are counted.

features.name: has_example_phrase_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain an example phrase such as 'for example', 'for instance' or 'e.g.'?
features.spec: df['example_phrase_comment_count'] > 0 as 1/0; null if `example_phrase_comment_count` is null.

decomposed.h0: has_example_phrase_comment has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with at least one counter-argument containing example phrases have higher delta rates.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the row's delta outcome (OP changed view), an association only. Comments are not individually linked to outcomes, so comparison is at discussion level: presence of example-phrase comments vs. none. Literal phrase matching only; it does not verify a real example is given. Comment text may include quoted material or outcome announcements, which are not excluded. Comment timing unknown. The count feature is an alternative intensity measure; its count scale depends on number of comments available.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with numbers or statistics are more persuasive

features.name: share_comments_with_numeric_evidence
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments use numbers or statistics in making their argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide whether the commenter themself uses a specific number, quantity, percentage, or statistic (e.g. data figures, rates, counts, study results) as part of their counter-argument. Incidental numbers (list numbering, 'two reasons', dates used only as labels, usernames, URLs) do not count; numbers or statistics in quotations of the OP or others count only if the commenter adopts them. Ignore any content announcing OP view change, delta awards, or outcome reports. Return (comments qualifying)/(total comments) in [0,1]. Null if OC_comments is missing or malformed; null if the list is empty.

features.name: any_comment_digit_present
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a numeral digit?
features.spec: import json; l=json.loads(df['OC_comments']); return null if missing/malformed; return int(any(re.search(r'\d', c) for c in l)); empty list gives 0. Raw text match: no semantic filtering, so digits in URLs, quotations or delta announcements count; outcome contamination possible.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_with_numeric_evidence has no association with whether the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_with_numeric_evidence is associated with a greater likelihood that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Comments are unordered with no per-comment outcomes, so the test is row-level share, not comparison of individual comments; association only, not causal. The digit-detector is a mechanical secondary measure (not in rhs) and may match URLs, quotes, or outcome announcements. OC_comments text is current text with unknown timing relative to the outcome.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that appeal to expertise or evidence (study, research, data, evidence) are more persuasive

features.name: share_comments_appeal_expertise_evidence
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments appeal to expertise or evidence (e.g., a study, research, data, cited evidence, or expert authority) in support of their own argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. For each comment decide whether the commenter themself appeals to expertise or evidence as support: citing or referring to a study, research, data/statistics, documented evidence, a source/link, or claimed expert authority (their own professional expertise or named experts). Use title/argument only to interpret the target. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it as support; quotations of the OP or background/rebuttal quotes do not count. Bare opinion, anecdote or logic without evidence/expertise appeals do not count. Ignore any statements that OP changed their view, delta awards, or reports of the outcome; these are not evidence of the construct (generic delta-rule discussion is neutral). Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed input gives null. List order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_appeal_expertise_evidence has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_appeal_expertise_evidence is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only. Comparison is implicit (share of evidence/expertise-appealing comments versus other comments). Comments are unordered with no timing; comment text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence. Share is a row-level aggregate; commenter identity not distinguished.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that quote the OP are less persuasive

features.name: share_comments_quoting_op
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments directly quote the OP's own title or argument text?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment, decide whether it directly quotes the OP's words (verbatim or near-verbatim excerpt from title or argument, e.g. markdown > blockquote or quotation marks reproducing OP's text), using title and argument to verify the quoted text is the OP's. Quotation of other sources, or paraphrase without quoted words, does not count. Ignore any quoted text that is an OP view-change/delta-award announcement or post-outcome resolution update; such text does not count as quoting. Output = number of comments quoting the OP divided by total number of comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; malformed/missing OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_quoting_op has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_quoting_op is associated with lower probability of delta (OP view change).
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view); associations only. Comments are unordered and have no per-comment outcomes, so the row-level share of quoting comments is used as a proxy for quoting counter-arguments; this is not a comparison of quoting vs non-quoting comments' persuasiveness within a row. Text is current and may include edits/outcome announcements, which the spec excludes from quote evidence. Rows with no comments are null.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with fewer absolutist words (always, never, certainly, obviously) are more persuasive

features.name: absolutist_word_share
features.definition: What proportion of all words across the counter-argument comments are absolutist words (always, never, certainly, obviously)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads (malformed/missing -> null). Join all comment strings; lowercase; tokenize words with re.findall(r"[a-z']+", text). Count tokens exactly equal to one of {always, never, certainly, obviously}. Return count / total tokens. Empty list or zero tokens -> null. Raw lexical match with no semantic filtering; quoted text and any outcome announcements in comments are included.

decomposed.h0: absolutist_word_share has no association with delta.
decomposed.h1: Higher absolutist_word_share in counter-arguments is associated with lower likelihood of delta (fewer absolutist words, more persuasive).
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). The word list is limited to the four given examples, as the hypothesis lists them and gives no wider lexicon; share normalizes for comment length. Comments are pooled across all counter-arguments, and quoted text is not separated from the commenter's own words. Comment timing is unknown, and comments may contain outcome-related text. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with more positive sentiment are more persuasive

features.name: counterarg_mean_positive_sentiment
features.definition: What is the average sentiment positivity of the counter-argument comments, from very negative to very positive?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Rate each comment's overall sentiment expressed in the commenter's own words on an integer scale: -2 very negative, -1 negative, 0 neutral/mixed, 1 positive, 2 very positive. Ignore quoted text from others unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks for changing view, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome; do not use them as sentiment evidence. Return the mean across comments with a rating. Empty list gives null; malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: Counter-argument mean positive sentiment has no association with the probability the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher counterarg_mean_positive_sentiment is associated with higher probability of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta. Sentiment scale (-2..2) and mean aggregation are operational assumptions; "counter-arguments" are all OC_comments, whose order and timing are unknown. Comments may contain post-outcome text, which the prompt excludes from sentiment evidence. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with lower negative sentiment are more persuasive (calmer tone wins)

features.name: mean_negative_sentiment_of_counterarguments
features.definition: On average across the counter-argument comments, how negative is the sentiment or tone of each comment's own wording?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). For each comment, rate the negative sentiment of the commenter's own assertions on an integer 0-4 scale: 0 = calm/neutral or positive, no negativity; 1 = slight negativity; 2 = moderate (clear criticism, frustration); 3 = strong (hostile, sarcastic, insulting); 4 = extremely hostile or abusive. Do not rate text the commenter merely quotes from others (e.g., the OP) unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any statements that announce or report that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates; do not use them as evidence of tone. Generic discussion of delta rules is eligible. Return the arithmetic mean of the per-comment ratings across all comments. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed; return null if the list is empty (no comments to average).

decomposed.h0: mean_negative_sentiment_of_counterarguments has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Lower mean_negative_sentiment_of_counterarguments is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view (negative coefficient).
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). The 0-4 negativity rubric and the mean aggregation across comments are operational assumptions, since the hypothesis does not specify them. "Calmer tone" is treated as lower negative sentiment only. OC_comments are unordered and have no timestamps; comments may be reply-linked in unknown ways, and the current text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt is told to ignore. Associations only, not causal. The test is OLS on binary delta (linear probability model).

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with explicit disagreement words (wrong, incorrect, disagree) are less persuasive

features.name: any_comment_has_disagreement_word
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain an explicit disagreement word (wrong, incorrect, or disagree)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. Malformed/missing input -> null. Empty list -> 0. Otherwise 1 if any comment matches case-insensitive regex r'\b(wrong|incorrect|disagree)\b', else 0. Pure literal matching: no semantic filtering (negations, quotations, or outcome announcements are not excluded). Inflected forms like 'disagreed' or 'incorrectly' do not match.

features.name: share_comments_with_disagreement_word
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments contain an explicit disagreement word (wrong, incorrect, or disagree)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. Malformed/missing -> null. Empty list -> null. Otherwise share = (number of comments matching case-insensitive regex r'\b(wrong|incorrect|disagree)\b') / (total comments in list). Range 0-1. Literal matching only; no semantic filtering.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between share_comments_with_disagreement_word and the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_with_disagreement_word is associated with a lower probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: "Less persuasive" is operationalized as lower delta (OP view change) at the row level. Rows are discussions, not individual comments, so per-comment persuasiveness is unavailable; the share is a row-level proxy and any_comment_has_disagreement_word is an alternative exposure. The word list (wrong, incorrect, disagree) is matched literally on whole words, so negation, quotation of OP text, and other inflections are not distinguished. Comment order and timing are unknown. OC_comments may contain post-outcome text, including delta announcements; this is not filtered. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with less first-person language (I, me, my) are more persuasive (less anecdotal)

features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; if missing or malformed return null. Concatenate all comments. Tokenize words with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text.lower()). Count tokens in {'i','me','my'} (also count contractions I'm, I've, I'll, I'd as 'i' by tokens starting with "i'" ; exclude 'mine','myself'). Return count / total word tokens. The parenthetical 'less anecdotal' is only the rationale; anecdotes are not measured separately. Raw text may include quoted text from others or OP-change announcements (contamination/timing risk), and no comment timing is supplied. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with more second-person language (you, your) are more persuasive

Count tokens matching ^(you|your|yours|yourself|yourselves)$ or you're/you've/you'll/you'd. Result = total matched tokens across all comments / total tokens across all comments. Quoted OP text within comments is counted mechanically, as are possible delta announcements in raw text, so contamination is possible. features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with higher vocabulary diversity (type-token ratio) are more persuasive

features.name: mean_counterargument_ttr
features.definition: What is the average type-token ratio (unique words divided by total words) of the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of comment strings. For each comment, lowercase and tokenize with re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text.lower()); tokens = words. Comment TTR = len(set(tokens))/len(tokens); skip comments with zero tokens. Return the mean of comment TTRs across comments with at least one token. If the list is valid but empty (or no comment has tokens), return null; if malformed/missing, return null. No stemming or stopword removal. Raw text is used as is, so quoted text and any outcome announcements in comments are included; TTR is length-sensitive (shorter comments tend to have higher TTR).

Type-token ratio is computed per comment and averaged (the unit of aggregation is an assumption; pooling all comments would be an alternative). TTR strongly depends on comment length, and no length control is included, as it was not part of the claim. OC_comments is the available set of counter-comments; list order is not chronology, and comments may include post-outcome text because raw text is used. Tokenization is a simple regex assumption.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments with higher reading complexity (Flesch-Kincaid grade) are more persuasive

features.name: oc_fk_grade_mean
features.definition: What is the mean Flesch-Kincaid grade level across the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads; keep string comments with at least one word (regex [A-Za-z']+). For each, sentences = max(1, count of runs of [.!?]+ followed by space/end, fallback 1); words = count of [A-Za-z']+ tokens; syllables = sum over words of max(1, count of vowel groups [aeiouy]+ in lowercase word, minus 1 if word ends in silent 'e' and has >1 group). FK = 0.39*words/sentences + 11.8*syllables/words - 15.59. Return the mean FK across comments. Empty list gives null (no comments to score); malformed/missing gives null.

decomposed.h0: oc_fk_grade_mean has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_fk_grade_mean is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); the association is not causal. Mean FK across comments is an assumed aggregation, since the hypothesis does not specify one. FK is computed with a heuristic syllable counter, and URLs, quotes and markdown are not stripped. OC_comments may contain text that announces the outcome, such as delta awards, because this is raw-text code with no semantic filtering. Comment order and timing are unknown.

Use title/argument only to interpret what a comment targets. Count only the commenter's own assertions, not analogies merely quoted from the OP or others unless the commenter adopts them. Ignore mere figurative phrases without inference, and ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments by other users use analogical reasoning?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (list of comments by non-OP users). Numerator: comments that themselves argue by analogy (compare the issue to a different, similar case and draw an inference; cues like 'just like', 'analogous to' count only when they introduce a real analogy). Denominator: total comments in the list. Return numerator/denominator in [0,1]. Use title/argument only to interpret targets. Do not count analogies only quoted from others unless adopted by the commenter. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Null for empty list or missing/malformed input.

Analogy judged from current comment text; reply timing unknown; comments are unordered and there are no per-comment outcomes, so rows with an analogical comment may simply have more or longer comments. Both features are included in rhs, so the term estimates the any-analogy coefficient conditional on share; they are correlated. features.name: novel_content_word_types
features.definition: How many distinct content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) across the counter-argument comments do not appear anywhere in the OP's title or argument?

Content words defined by POS tags (NN, VB, JJ, RB) minus stopwords, lemma-matched; this is an assumed recipe. Conversation column not used to avoid overlap. Association only.

features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; if missing/malformed, return null; if the list is empty, return null. Tokenize text by lowercasing and extracting regex [a-z']+ tokens. Return the mean of per-comment overlaps across comments (equal weights, each comment counted once); null if no comment has a defined value. Raw text is used as supplied; no semantic filtering.
